audience: Accounts payable staff who need to know how much is outstanding with a vendor, and where that figure comes from.
goal: Find a vendor's **outstanding balance** and cross-check it three ways: from the vendor record (**Due** and **Partner Ledger**), from the **Aged Payable** report, and from the vendor's **bills**. The guide uses the vendor **Engineer - Production**.
before: You can open the **Accounting** app, with its **Vendors** and **Reporting** menus.
Your Odoo is on the company the vendor belongs to. A vendor that belongs to another company is invisible until you switch company (top right).
outcome: You have found the vendor and read their balance from the **Partner Ledger** (total debit and total credit).
You have found the same vendor in the **Aged Payable** report and read the **Total** column.
You have checked the vendor's bills to see whether any are still unpaid.
notes: The screenshots were captured by an automated run on a **test database**. The red banner at the top ("Database neutralized for testing") only appears on test databases. The figures are test data and will differ from yours.
This tour is **read-only**: it only looks at records and changes nothing.

In this data the vendor has **no bills**. Its balance comes from payments with no bill to match: the Partner Ledger shows total debit **1,001** and total credit **1**, and Aged Payable shows **−1,000** (a negative payable means we paid the vendor in advance, so the vendor owes us).

The **Due** smart button on the vendor record only appears for a vendor we still owe money to. In this data the vendor's follow-up balance is nil, so the button is absent and the guide's steps for it are descriptive only.
The vendor is listed in **Aged Payable** only because its balance is not zero. A vendor with a nil balance does not appear in that report.

phases.title: Find the vendor
phases.summary: Search the vendor master list and open the vendor record.

phases.title: Read the balance on the vendor record
phases.summary: Use the smart buttons and the Partner Ledger.
phases.checkpoint: You have read the debit and credit totals in the Partner Ledger.

phases.title: Check the Aged Payable report
phases.summary: See the vendor's balance by age.
phases.checkpoint: You have found the vendor in **Aged Payable** and read the **Total** column.

phases.title: Check the bills behind the balance
phases.summary: Open the vendor bills filtered to this vendor.
phases.checkpoint: You know whether the vendor has any bills, and their payment status.

glossary.meaning: What is still unpaid between you and the vendor.
A button at the top of a record that shows a figure (such as **Invoiced**) and opens the related records.
Every posted accounting entry for one partner, with total debit and credit. The difference between them is the balance.
The two sides of an accounting entry. For a vendor, bills are credits (we owe) and payments are debits (we paid).
A report that groups what you owe each vendor by how overdue it is.
A negative figure in Aged Payable means the vendor owes **you**, for example because you paid before receiving a bill.

1.title: Open the Accounting app
1.do: On the Odoo home screen, click the **Accounting** app.
actions: Go to the Odoo home screen.
1.see: The Accounting app opens with its menu bar across the top.
1.why: Every vendor balance is found from the Accounting app.

2.title: Open the Vendors menu
2.do: In the top menu bar, click **Vendors**.
actions: Look at the menu bar across the top.
2.see: A drop-down with the vendor entries, including **Bills**, **Payments** and **Vendors**.
2.why: This menu holds the vendor master, bills and payments.

3.title: Open the Vendors list
3.see: The **Vendors** master list, shown as cards.
3.why: The vendor master is where every supplier record is kept.

4.title: Search for the vendor
4.do: Type the vendor's name in the search box and press **Enter**.
actions: Click the search box at the top.
If a **Vendor Bills** filter is showing, remove it with its **×**; it hides vendors that have no bills.
4.see: The vendor's card, with the name you typed shown as a filter in the search box.
4.why: Searching narrows the list down to one vendor.
4.tip: If nothing is found, check the company selected at the top right. A vendor that belongs to another company is hidden.

5.title: Open the vendor record
5.do: Click the vendor's card to open it.
5.see: The vendor's record, with a row of smart buttons across the top.
5.why: The smart buttons on the record give the vendor's key figures.

6.title: Open the More smart buttons
6.do: Click **More** in the row of smart buttons.
actions: Look at the row of smart buttons at the top.
6.see: A short menu with **Partner Ledger** and other entries.
6.why: The accounting smart buttons (**Due**, **Invoiced** and **Partner Ledger**) are grouped here and in the row beside it.
6.tip: **Due** appears only for a vendor we still owe money to.

7.title: Read the Due amount
7.do: Look for the **Due** smart button and read its figure.
actions: Look along the smart buttons for **Due**.
If it is there, read the figure and click it to see the open items and **Total Due**.
If it is not there, the vendor has nothing due.
7.see: The **Due** figure is the vendor's outstanding balance straight from the vendor record. In this data the button is absent because the due amount is nil.
7.why: It is the quickest way to see what you owe a vendor.
7.warning: A missing **Due** button does not mean the vendor has no entries at all. Check the Partner Ledger below.

8.title: Go back to the vendor record
8.do: If you opened the **Due** screen, click the vendor's name in the breadcrumb at the top left.
actions: Look at the breadcrumb at the top left.
Click the vendor's name to go back.
8.why: You return to the record to reach the next smart button.

9.title: Open More again
actions: Click **More** in the smart buttons row.
9.why: You are reaching the Partner Ledger.

10.title: Open the Partner Ledger
10.see: A list of **Journal Items** filtered to this vendor, with the filters **Posted** and **Payable or Receivable**.
10.why: It shows every posted entry for this vendor and the running outstanding balance.

11.title: Read the Partner Ledger total
11.do: Read the **Debit** and **Credit** totals in the footer row.
actions: Look at the bottom of the list, at the row outlined in red.
points: Here the debit is higher, so the vendor owes **us**.
A bill adds to the credit; a payment adds to the debit.
11.see: Two totals. The difference between them is the outstanding balance.
11.why: The ledger is the most detailed view: you can see every entry that makes up the balance.
11.tip: Open a line's **Journal Entry** to see the bill or payment behind it.

12.title: Open the Reporting menu
12.do: In the top menu bar, click **Reporting**.
12.see: A drop-down listing the Accounting reports.
12.why: **Aged Payable** is the standard way to see what is outstanding to vendors, by age.

13.title: Open Aged Payable
13.do: In the **Partner Reports** group, click **Aged Payable**.
13.where: Accounting app > Reporting > Partner Reports > Aged Payable
actions: Wait for the report to load.
13.see: The **Aged Payable** report, listing each vendor with the amount split into age columns.
13.why: It lists every vendor with an open balance, split into **At Date, 1-30, 31-60, 61-90, 91-120** and **Older**.

14.title: Read the vendor row
14.do: Find the vendor's row and read across to the **Total** column.
actions: Find **Engineer - Production** in the list (outlined in red).
points: The **Total** is the outstanding payable at the report date.
A negative figure means the vendor owes you, for example after a payment in advance.
A vendor with a nil balance does not appear.
14.see: The vendor's row, with its balance in the **Older** and **Total** columns (−1,000 in this data).
14.why: The figure should agree with the Partner Ledger (debit minus credit, with the sign reversed).
14.tip: If the two disagree, check the report's **As of** date and the company.

15.title: Open the Vendors menu again
15.do: In the top menu bar, click **Vendors**.
15.why: You now check the bills behind the balance.

16.title: Open Bills
16.why: The bill list shows what is still unpaid, bill by bill.

17.title: Filter the bills by vendor
17.do: Type the vendor's name in the search box and press **Enter**.
17.see: The bill list narrows to this vendor's bills, or shows an empty list if there are none.
17.why: It keeps only this vendor's bills.

18.title: Check the bills behind the balance
18.do: Read the **Payment** and **Status** columns of the list.
actions: Read **Total** for the amount of each bill.
points: **Payment** and **Status** show which bills are still open.
**Total** is the amount of each bill.
18.see: In this data the list is **empty**: the vendor has no bills.
18.why: If no bills appear, the balance seen earlier comes from an unmatched payment, not from an unpaid bill.
18.tip: That completes the tour: find the vendor, read the ledger, check Aged Payable, and check the bills.
